provenance: Headline recall figures, verbatim from Baker et al. (OpenAI 2025), 'Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation': while a frontier coding agent trains with RL, a GPT-4o monitor that reads the agent's chain of thought catches ~95% of systemic reward hacks, versus ~60% for a monitor that sees only actions/outputs. When the training reward directly penalizes 'bad thoughts', the agent learns OBFUSCATED reward hacking: it still hacks at a rate comparable to before, but stops verbalizing intent, and CoT-monitor recall collapses to near zero. points x: optimization pressure on the CoT (0 = none, 10 = strong), y = CoT-monitor recall %, endpoints pinned to the paper's two regimes (95% -> ~0%). The curve between the endpoints (logistic collapse, fit.params cliff/steep) and the task-reward curve (rewardStart -> rewardEnd, unitless) are authored illustrations of the paper's qualitative dynamics, not digitized training curves; the page labels them as such.
